title: Five minutes at the door
summary: Step outside, or stand in an open doorway or on a balcony, and notice what is around you for five minutes.
objective: Spend a small, real stretch of time in outdoor air and pay attention to it.
steps: Go to a door, balcony, step or yard. Standing just inside an open door counts if going out is hard today.
Set a five-minute timer and put your phone away.
Name three sounds, two things that are moving and one thing you can smell or feel on your skin.
completionCriteria: You spent five minutes at an open door or outdoors.
You named three sounds.
tip: This is the smallest quest on purpose. Doing it on a hard day is a perfectly good result.

indoorFallback.title: Open-window pause
indoorFallback.summary: Open a window wide, sit beside it for five minutes and name three sounds you can hear.

title: Name three birds
summary: Spot three different birds and describe each one: size, colour, sound, behaviour.
objective: Practise slow, close observation of the living things nearest to you.
steps: Walk to the nearest tree, hedge or water and stand still for two minutes.
Write or say what you see and hear. Guesses are fine.
Find three different birds and note one detail about each.
completionCriteria: You stayed in one spot for at least two minutes.
You described three different birds.
tip: A bird you cannot name still counts. Describe it and look it up later.

indoorFallback.title: Listen from a window
indoorFallback.summary: Open a window and note three bird sounds or movements. Describe each one in a sentence.

title: Cloud spotter
summary: Watch the sky for ten minutes and describe how it changes.
objective: Slow down by following one thing in the sky from start to finish.
steps: Find a spot with a wide view of the sky.
Pick one cloud and follow it for five minutes.
Note how its shape, colour or speed changed.
completionCriteria: You watched one cloud (or the sky) for five minutes.
You noted at least one change.

indoorFallback.title: Window sky watch
indoorFallback.summary: Sit by a window with a clear view of the sky and follow one cloud for five minutes.

title: Leaf detective
summary: Look closely at five different leaves and sort them by one feature you choose.
objective: Notice variety in the plants around you by comparing them carefully.
steps: Walk to the nearest trees, bushes or a patch of weeds.
Find five leaves that look different. Look at edges, size and vein patterns. Fallen leaves are fine to pick up.
Group them by one feature of your choice and note which group is biggest.
completionCriteria: You looked closely at five different leaves.
You sorted them by one feature.
tip: Leave living plants intact and wash your hands afterwards. Do not taste anything you find.

indoorFallback.title: Houseplant leaf study
indoorFallback.summary: Compare the leaves of three houseplants or kitchen herbs: shape, texture, edges.

title: Sound map
summary: Sit still and draw a simple map of every sound you hear, placed by direction.
objective: Turn listening into a small, concrete observation task.
steps: Sit somewhere you can stay for five minutes. Draw a dot in the middle of a page for yourself.
Each time you hear a sound, mark its direction with a symbol or a word.
After five minutes, look at your map and circle the sound you liked most.
equipment: Paper and pen, or a notes app
completionCriteria: You sat still for five minutes.
You recorded at least eight sounds.

indoorFallback.title: Sound map from a window
indoorFallback.summary: Do the same sound map from beside an open window for ten minutes.

title: Light and shadow
summary: Take five photos where the light is the subject, not the object.
objective: Train your eye to notice light, one photo at a time.
steps: Walk somewhere with trees, buildings or railings.
Photograph five different shadows or patches of light.
Pick your favourite and notice what made it work.
completionCriteria: You took five photos focused on light or shadow.
You picked a favourite.
tip: Low sun makes long shadows. Early morning and late afternoon are best.

indoorFallback.title: Window light study
indoorFallback.summary: Photograph five patterns of light or shadow that fall inside your home.

title: Closer than usual
summary: Photograph three small things up close: bark, a petal, a stone, a seed head.
objective: See familiar places differently by getting close.
steps: Choose a patch of ground or a single tree.
Move slowly and look for texture and pattern.
Take three close-ups from different angles.
completionCriteria: You took three close-up photos.
Each one is from a different angle.

indoorFallback.title: Close-ups at home
indoorFallback.summary: Photograph three small textures indoors: fabric, a plant leaf, a wooden surface.

title: Colour hunt
summary: Pick one colour and find ten things in that colour while you are outside.
objective: Turn an ordinary outing into a game of looking.
steps: Choose a colour before you go out.
Walk anywhere you like and spot things in that colour.
Photograph or note at least three of the ten things you found.
equipment: Phone or camera, or just your eyes
completionCriteria: You found ten things in your colour.
You recorded three of them.
tip: Good with children. Let them choose the colour.

indoorFallback.title: Colour hunt at home
indoorFallback.summary: Find ten things in your colour inside your home and arrange three of them together.

title: Sketch a view
summary: Draw one outdoor view for fifteen minutes. Rough is fine.
objective: Look at one scene long enough to really see it.
steps: Find a place to sit with a view you like.
Sketch the main shapes first, then add detail for fifteen minutes.
Write the date and place on the page.
completionCriteria: You drew one view for at least fifteen minutes.
You finished it, however rough.
tip: No one has to see it. The looking is the point.

indoorFallback.title: Sketch from a window
indoorFallback.summary: Sketch the view from a window for twenty minutes.

title: Seed to sprout
summary: Plant something small outdoors or on a balcony and set a reminder to check it.
objective: Start something growing and give yourself a reason to come back outside.
steps: Choose a pot or patch and fill it with soil.
Plant a seed or cutting.
Water it and note a day to check on it.
completionCriteria: You planted something.
You picked a day to check on it.
tip: Herbs like basil, mint and coriander are forgiving for beginners.

indoorFallback.title: Windowsill sprout
indoorFallback.summary: Plant a seed in a small container on a bright indoor windowsill and note a day to check it.

title: Tend a patch
summary: Spend half an hour weeding, watering or tidying one growing space.
objective: Give steady care to one small piece of green space.
steps: Pick one bed, pot group or window box.
Remove weeds and dead leaves.
Water at the base of the plants.
equipment: Small trowel or just your hands
completionCriteria: You worked on one growing space for at least twenty minutes.
You removed weeds or dead leaves and watered.
tip: Take breaks. Kneeling pads and a low stool make this much easier on the body.

indoorFallback.title: Houseplant tidy
indoorFallback.summary: Remove dead leaves, wipe dust off, and water a few houseplants.

title: Pollinator water stop
summary: Set up a shallow dish with pebbles and fresh water for bees and other insects.
objective: Make a small, practical contribution to local wildlife.
steps: Choose a shaded or part-shaded spot you can see from a window or door.
Fill a shallow dish with pebbles so insects have somewhere to land.
Add water to just below the top of the pebbles, and note a day to refresh it.
completionCriteria: You set up the dish in a safe spot.
You chose a day to refresh the water.
tip: Change the water every few days so it does not become a place for mosquitoes to breed.

indoorFallback.title: Plan a pollinator pot
indoorFallback.summary: Sketch which flowering plants you could grow in one pot and where it would sit.

title: Compost starter
summary: Start a small compost caddy or bin with kitchen scraps and dry leaves or paper.
objective: Set up a simple habit that reduces waste.
steps: Pick a container with a lid, or check what your area offers for food-waste collection.
Layer vegetable scraps with dry leaves or torn paper.
Put it somewhere convenient and note what you can and cannot add.
completionCriteria: You set up a container or confirmed a collection option.
You wrote down what to add.
tip: Avoid meat, dairy and cooked food in a basic home compost.

indoorFallback.title: Find your local options
indoorFallback.summary: Look up what your local council accepts for food waste and garden waste.

title: Phone-away walk
summary: Walk for twenty minutes with your phone in a bag or pocket, no headphones.
objective: Walk without a screen so you can notice what is around you.
steps: Set a timer, then put the phone away.
Walk any route you like.
When the timer ends, note one thing you noticed that you would have missed.
equipment: A bag or pocket for your phone
completionCriteria: You walked for twenty minutes with your phone away.
You noted one thing you noticed.
tip: If you need your phone for safety or maps, keep it on silent and pocketed.

indoorFallback.title: Slow walk at home
indoorFallback.summary: Walk slowly around your home for ten minutes with your phone in another room and notice sounds and light.

title: Two stops farther
summary: Get off public transport two stops early, or park farther away, and walk the rest.
objective: Add a short walk to a trip you were making anyway.
steps: Check that the walk is safe and well-lit.
Get off early or park farther away.
Walk the rest and notice something new on the route.
equipment: Transport pass if you need one
completionCriteria: You added a walk of at least fifteen minutes to a trip.
You noticed something new on the route.

indoorFallback.title: Stairs and stretch break
indoorFallback.summary: Use stairs instead of a lift where you can, then do a short stretch by an open window.

title: Ten-minute loop
summary: Walk five minutes in any direction, turn around, and walk back.
objective: Make a short outing as simple as possible.
steps: Put on shoes and set a timer for ten minutes.
Walk out for five minutes at a comfortable pace, then turn around.
Notice one thing on the way back that you did not see on the way out.
completionCriteria: You walked for ten minutes in total.
You noticed one new thing.
tip: Go as slowly as you like. A slow ten minutes is still ten minutes outside.

indoorFallback.title: Ten minutes of gentle movement indoors
indoorFallback.summary: Walk slowly through your home and stretch for ten minutes with a window open.

title: Gentle stretch outside
summary: Do a few easy stretches or slow movements in fresh air.
objective: Combine light movement with being outdoors.
steps: Find a flat spot outside, or stand in a doorway if that is easier.
Do five or six gentle movements within your comfortable range: reach up, roll your shoulders, bend gently to each side.
Finish with five slow breaths and notice the air.
completionCriteria: You moved gently for at least ten minutes.
You stayed within your comfortable range.
tip: Stop if anything hurts. This is not a workout and is not medical advice.

indoorFallback.title: Stretch by an open window
indoorFallback.summary: Do the same gentle stretches beside an open window for ten minutes.

title: Pick up ten
summary: Collect ten pieces of litter from your street or a nearby park and dispose of them properly.
objective: Leave one small patch of your neighbourhood cleaner than you found it.
steps: Bring gloves and a bag.
Avoid sharp or hazardous items and report them instead.
Dispose of the litter in a bin and wash your hands.
completionCriteria: You collected ten pieces of litter.
You disposed of them properly and avoided hazardous items.

indoorFallback.title: Sort your recycling
indoorFallback.summary: Check your recycling and rubbish bins at home and sort items correctly.

title: Say hello to a neighbour
summary: Greet someone nearby and ask them one question about the area.
objective: Make one small, friendly connection close to home.
steps: Go outside where neighbours are likely to be.
Say hello and introduce yourself if you have not met.
Ask one question: a favourite local spot, or how long they have lived there.
completionCriteria: You greeted someone nearby.
You asked one question, or smiled and nodded if that felt right.
tip: Only do this if it feels comfortable. A smile and a nod still counts.

indoorFallback.title: Write a note
indoorFallback.summary: Write a short friendly note or message to a neighbour or friend you have not spoken to lately.

title: Thank a local worker
summary: Thank someone who keeps your neighbourhood running: a delivery rider, bus driver, street cleaner or shopkeeper.
objective: Notice and appreciate the people who work outdoors around you.
steps: Pick a moment when the person is not rushed.
Say thank you and name one specific thing they do that helps.
Leave it there. No reply is needed.
completionCriteria: You thanked someone in person.
You named one specific thing.

indoorFallback.title: Write a thank-you message
indoorFallback.summary: Write a thank-you message to someone who helped you this week.

title: Report one thing
summary: Walk your street, spot one fixable problem such as a broken light or blocked path, and report it.
objective: Use a short walk to look after a shared space.
steps: Walk around your block or a nearby park and look for something that needs fixing.
Take a photo if you can do so without including people.
Report it through your local council's website or app, or note it down to report later.
equipment: Phone for a photo or report
completionCriteria: You found one real issue.
You reported it or wrote down where to report it.

indoorFallback.title: Report an issue you remember
indoorFallback.summary: Think of a local problem you have noticed recently and look up how to report it.

title: Walk and talk
summary: Invite someone to walk and chat instead of meeting indoors or on a call.
objective: Spend time with another person while moving at an easy pace outdoors.
steps: Invite one person and agree on a short route and a time.
Walk at the pace of whoever is slowest, with phones away.
Finish with a quick sit-down or a drink if you both want one.
completionCriteria: You walked with at least one other person for twenty minutes.
You talked or listened more than you scrolled.

indoorFallback.title: Tea by the window
indoorFallback.summary: Share a drink beside an open window instead, in person or on a call.

title: Shared picnic
summary: Share a simple picnic with friends, family or neighbours.
objective: Make a meal an excuse to sit outside together.
steps: Pick a spot and a time, and ask each person to bring one thing.
Spread out something to sit on and eat slowly.
Take all your rubbish home with you.
completionCriteria: You shared food outdoors for at least thirty minutes.
You took all your rubbish with you.

indoorFallback.title: Floor picnic
indoorFallback.summary: Spread a blanket by a window and share the same food indoors.

title: Outdoor I-spy
summary: Play a no-equipment game outside: I-spy, a scavenger list or a simple tag.
objective: Play together outdoors with almost no preparation.
steps: Choose a simple game everyone knows or write a short list of things to find.
Play for at least twenty minutes.
Let the youngest or slowest player set the pace.
equipment: Optional: a written list and pencil
completionCriteria: You played for at least twenty minutes.
Everyone who wanted to join could take part.

indoorFallback.title: Window I-spy
indoorFallback.summary: Play I-spy using only what you can see through a window.

title: Group tidy-up
summary: Do a small group clean-up or planting session in a shared outdoor space.
objective: Do something useful for a shared space together.
steps: Invite two or three people or join a local event, and agree on one small area.
Bring gloves and bags, and check you may work there.
Work for around forty-five minutes, then share a drink.
completionCriteria: You spent at least thirty minutes on a shared outdoor task with another person.
You left the space tidy and disposed of waste properly.
tip: Skip sharp, hazardous or unknown items and report them instead.

indoorFallback.title: Plan the day
indoorFallback.summary: Message three people, pick a date and choose a small area to look after.
